transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-19
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Atlas Head of ML), Priya Shah (Atlas PM), Tom Wu (Atlas DevOps), Jordan Lee (Atlas DS)

Summary: quick product walkthrough of Redwood's Eval/Quality Monitoring (Console + API + Optimize). Focus on prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons and running an initial pilot. Atlas is running multitenant commerce LLM features (recommendations, merchandising copy); wants to reduce regressions after model updates and get automated alerts tied to prompt sets.

Topics: product walkthrough, prompt set design, A/B comparison workflows, regression alerting thresholds, data residency/ops question (VPC/KMS), pilot scope & next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. im Maya from Redwood, AE. we'll keep this to 30-45, mostly a walkthrough of eval and quality monitoring, then we can dig into questions.
[00:07] Alex: great thanks, maya. im Alex, head of ML at Atlas. quick context: we run a few LLM-powered features in prod — product descriptions, personalized promo copy, and a search ranking reranker. after model updates we sometimes see regressions in tone and hallucinations, so we're looking for automated alerts + easy A/B comparisons.
[00:22] Priya: hi, im Priya, product. timeline: we'd like to start a pilot in september if feasible. budget ok, but need clear success metrics.
[00:30] Liam: awesome. so high level, Redwood's eval/quality monitoring lets you define prompt sets — those are like canonical prompts + expected outputs or metrics — then we run prompt sets against model versions and produce regression alerts. we support A/B comparisons via per-route rollouts in the Console and API side-by-side dashboards.
[00:45] Jordan: can you show the console?
[00:47] Liam: sure, pulling up Console. (small pause) ok here's the Project view, you can see routes for each product: copy-gen, reranker, search-suggest. Under Eval we have 'prompt sets' — you can create sets from examples, upload a CSV, or import from our SDK. each sample can have metadata: expected label, tolerance for numeric metrics, acceptable tokens, and a rubric.
[01:15] Alex: on the rubric, can we do both fuzzy match and semantic similarity for nlg? we use BLEU sometimes but want more nuance.
[01:24] Liam: yes, you can define multiple metrics per sample: token overlap, embedding cosine threshold, custom LLM-based classifier (you can plug in a human-in-the-loop labeler). caution: the LLM classifier adds cost. also we provide fuzzy string match and a normalized semantic similarity using embeddings.
[01:42] Priya: how do regression alerts surface? email? slack?
[01:45] Liam: configurable — Slack, PagerDuty, webhook, or email. alerts are triggered when a metric falls outside the configured guardrail for X consecutive runs, or if overall quality delta exceeds a threshold. We also include per-sample diffs and a traffic-weighted score so you don't get noise from low-volume prompts.
[02:05] Tom: what's the cadence of runs? real-time? daily?
[02:07] Liam: flexible — you can run prompt sets on every deployment, on a schedule (e.g., hourly/daily), or continuously via streaming checks. For pilot we'd usually run a nightly full sweep plus smoke checks on deploy.
[02:20] Alex: what about A/B comparisons? we need to compare model A vs model B on the same prompt set with significance testing.
[02:28] Liam: yep. In the Console's A/B tab you can pick two model versions or two routes. we compute paired-sample statistics with bootstrap confidence intervals for metrics, and we flag meaningful deltas. there's also a side-by-side sample viewer so you can inspect outputs per prompt.
[02:45] Jordan: do you do automatic grouping for similar prompts? we have many near-duplicates generated by UI flows.
[02:51] Liam: we have clustering by embedding similarity and metadata tags; you can group by intent and aggregate metrics by group. helps reduce alert fatigue.
[03:00] Maya: quick note on integrations: we can pull sample traffic from your logs (S3, GCS) or instrument the Redwood SDK to capture production calls with PII redaction. For Atlas, if you want private deployment, Redwood Private supports VPC peering and KMS integration for key management.
[03:18] Tom: we need SOC2 and audit logs — is that supported?
[03:21] Liam: yes, Dedicated and Private tiers have audit logs, retention controls, SSO (SAML/Okta), and SOC2 cert. We'll share the security pack.
[03:30] Priya: show me a demo run?
[03:33] Liam: yeah; doing a demo using a synthetic prompt set. (screen changes) here's a prompt set for promo copy, 50 samples. we run it against model v1.4 and then v1.5 candidate. running now... (typing sounds)
[03:52] Liam: results populating — you can see per-sample score, overall MRR of metrics, and a small visualization: red bars where diffs exceed thresholds. sample viewer on the right shows model outputs inline and highlight differences.
[04:08] Alex: i see a bunch of small drift. can we get regression alerts only for production-weighted prompts?
[04:12] Liam: yes, filter by traffic weight, and you can set guards per-route. Also we support baseline windows — only compare to a frozen baseline to avoid cascading rollouts.
[04:24] Jordan: what about automated canarying? we'd like to run a canary for 1% traffic for a week and get auto rollback if quality hits an X% drop.
[04:32] Liam: built-in canary rollouts: you can configure policy to auto-fallback when quality drops below threshold or when error rates increase. policies are pluggable in the rollout config.
[04:42] Priya: do you capture costs per-eval? our finance team will ask for impact.
[04:46] Liam: yes, cost per sample and projected monthly eval cost by cadence. that's in the Optimize tab where we also show batching and quantization suggestions for reducing eval cost.
[04:56] Alex: curious about false positives — how noisy are alerts?
[04:59] Liam: depends on prompt set quality. we recommend calibration: start with broader thresholds, then tighten. use grouping, traffic-weighting, and a human review queue. we also have 'regression replay' where you can re-run failing samples with random seeds to check for flakiness.
[05:15] Jordan: what's the SDK like for running evals? we use Python and go.
[05:19] Liam: SDKs for Python, Node, and a CLI. quick example: import redwood_eval; upload_prompt_set; run_eval; results via API or webhook. We provide a runbook and a benchmark spreadsheet with sample sizes for statistical significance.
[05:33] Alex: network / data residency question — can eval data leave our VPC?
[05:36] Liam: for Private we can keep evals in your VPC or use an on-prem runner. For Dedicated we have VPC peering and customer-managed KMS so plaintext doesn't leave your controls. We'll detail that in the security doc.
[05:49] Priya: any customers doing A/B for reranking specifically?
[05:52] Maya: yes, a few retailers use reranker A/B with offline NDCG metrics plus online CTR. They use our A/B test dashboard to correlate eval deltas with business metrics.
[06:02] Tom: we have a separate concern: prompts are generated client-side by our UI, so sometimes inputs vary. can prompt sets account for input normalization?
[06:10] Liam: prompt normalization rules are supported; you can preprocess via the SDK or apply normalization templates in Console so samples match production inputs.
[06:20] Jordan: about alerts again, can we route certain alerts to the SRE team versus PMs?
[06:24] Liam: yes, per-alert routing by severity or tag. You can have 'sre' webhooks and 'product' slack channels separate.
[06:30] Priya: any demo of the API to trigger an eval on deploy?
[06:33] Liam: small code snippet: POST /evals with prompt_set_id and model_version; callback to your webhook. I'll paste that after the call.
[06:40] Alex: what are recommended sample sizes for A/B significance?
[06:43] Liam: depends on effect size. our benchmark spreadsheet has rules of thumb: for typical NLG metrics, 200-500 paired samples gives reasonable power for medium effects; we also support bootstrapping to estimate CIs.
[06:55] Maya: real quick cost estimate for pilot: for 10k evals nightly, with mixed metrics, typical spend is X — (gives ballpark) we'll put exact numbers in pricing.
[07:05] Priya: ok, pilot scope ideas?
[07:07] Maya: suggested pilot: 4 weeks, focus on promo-copy and reranker routes. Atlas provides 3 canonical prompt sets and a week of sample traffic. Redwood will run nightly evals, set up alerts, and run a canary for model v1.5. deliverables: dashboard access, weekly check-in, benchmark spreadsheet, security pack.
[07:26] Alex: sounds good. What do you need from us to get started?
[07:29] Liam: sample prompt sets (CSV), S3 path for traffic sample, contact for SSO setup if using Dedicated/Private, and which routing channels for alerts.
[07:37] Jordan: I'll upload prompt sets and a sample to the S3 bucket by friday.
[07:40] Maya: perfect. we'll follow up with SOW and pricing.
[07:43] Tom: last ops Q: any infra changes needed on our side for canary?
[07:47] Liam: minimal — we just need to install SDK or set up routing on the edge if you want client-side routing; otherwise Redwood handles routing. For Private there's an infra package but we'll coordinate with your infra team.
[07:58] Priya: thanks, this was helpful.
[08:00] Maya: recap and next steps: 1) Maya sends SOW/pricing and security pack by 2025-08-22; 2) Liam shares eval runbook and benchmark spreadsheet; 3) Atlas uploads prompt sets and sample traffic by 2025-08-23; 4) schedule pilot kick-off for week of 2025-09-01.
[08:20] Alex: thanks everyone.
[08:22] End of call.
